clue.text: Puss has family in the pussywillow

definitions.note: a description of where the thing is found, standing in for the noun

parts.note: puss is a pet name for a cat
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A cat and its relations have taken up residence in a willow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it says where the thing grows rather than what it is. The fluffy flower spikes of the pussy willow are the classic example.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft furry flower spikes of the pussy willow are the best-known example of this kind of hanging flower cluster.

clue.text: Leap out finally abandoning drophead coupe

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter named is left out of the car's name

parts.note: a cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, a drophead coupe

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word out

explanation.surface: A driver leaps out of a convertible at the end of the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out finally' is T, and 'abandoning' drops it from CABRIOLET. In ballet a cabriole is a leap with the legs beaten together.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet the term names a jump in which one leg is beaten against the other in the air.

clue.text: Horse's foot

definitions.meaning: a horse bred and trained for trotting races
a pig's foot cooked as food

explanation.definitionFit: A trotting-race horse is so called, and a pig's foot served as food also bears the name.

clue.text: To lodge in a hotel, worker must be cross

indicators.note: in means the lodging word is put inside the hotel word

parts.note: an inn is a hotel
to dig is to lodge, as in living in digs
the ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A labourer staying in a hotel is told he has to be angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' is British slang for lodgings, so to dig is to lodge; 'in' tells you where it goes. 'cross' is angry, not a crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross at unfair treatment is being angry with a sense of grievance, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: It's really bad if one is in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters of these words are in disarray and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that things are truly grim if a person gets into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'in trouble', acting on BAD IF ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in good faith, so genuine or real, used here as a stand-in for really.

clue.text: But hero had not then moved

indicators.note: moved means the letters of these four words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest that the hero had not in fact shifted position at that time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' signals the anagram of HERO HAD NOT THEN, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a contrasting point, doing the same work as the conjunction however.

clue.text: A divine ruler, an unpleasant crawler

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a divine or clergyman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, a ruler

explanation.surface: A list of a holy king alongside a nasty creeping creature.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen in crosswords (Elizabeth Regina), and DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine.
explanation.definitionFit: The snake is a venomous serpent that moves along the ground, so a crawler few people like.

clue.text: One group of soldiers fix up what it represents

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the TA, Territorial Army, is a body of British reserve soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for fix is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nail is to fix in place

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers is asked to repair the thing it stands for.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is the abbreviation for this nationality, so it is 'what it represents'. 'up' turns NAIL to LIAN after I and TA.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation It. or IT stands for the nationality and language of Rome, hence what the two letters represent.

clue.text: Guy's efficiency reduced by 60% --- Guy's disheartened

indicators.note: reduced by sixty per cent means only the opening four of the ten letters of efficiency are kept
disheartened means the middle letter, the heart, is removed from the word Guy

parts.note: the word Guy, with the apostrophe s left aside
U is the middle letter, the heart, of the word Guy

explanation.surface: A man's productivity has dropped sharply and he has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy is an effigy of Guy Fawkes burnt on British bonfire night, 5 November. Keeping 40% of EFFICIENCY leaves EFFI; 'disheartened' takes the heart U from GUY, leaving GY.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a stuffed figure of Guy Fawkes, so a crude human figure made to be burnt or mocked.

clue.text: Overcrowded slum finally has resort to a Company man

indicators.note: finally has means the slum word is followed at its end by the resort word

parts.note: a warren is a crowded maze of mean dwellings
Hastings is a seaside resort on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: A rundown district ends up with a holiday town given to a man from the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Company' is the East India Company; this man was its first Governor-General of India.
explanation.definitionFit: He served the East India Company and became the first Governor-General of Bengal and British India.

clue.text: Sow in spacious shed

parts.note: broad means wide or spacious
cast means shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: Someone plants seeds inside a roomy garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building but is the verb, as a snake casts or sheds its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattering seed by hand over a wide area is the original meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Leading characters in drama will avoid reckless film stunt

indicators.note: the leading characters are the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Actors in a play will steer clear of a dangerous movie stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunt' looks like a noun for a daredevil feat but is the verb meaning to hold back growth.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something's growth so it stays small is to stunt it.

clue.text: A whole plant outside, say

indicators.note: outside means the word for plant goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to plant in the ground
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: An entire plant is growing outdoors, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a noun but is the verb to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number, with no fraction, is the mathematical term.

clue.text: Making a mistake about a sleeper

indicators.note: about means the word for making a mistake goes around the letter

parts.note: erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone has got something wrong about a person who is asleep or a railway tie.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeper is a small ring worn to keep a newly pierced ear open, not someone asleep or a railway tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a plain ring kept in a pierced ear lobe so the hole does not close.

clue.text: Insect right in the middle of rock

indicators.note: in the middle of means the letter for right is put at the centre of the rock word

parts.note: lava is molten rock, and the rock it sets into

explanation.surface: A bug sits exactly in the centre of a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The grub stage of an insect is its early, wingless form, which is how it can stand for the creature.

clue.text: Stick around quarters and observe what follows

indicators.note: around means the stick word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a baton is a stick
the compass quarters east, north and east together give a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Wait about the barracks and watch the next event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the reversal of the stick word, giving NOTAB. 'quarters' are compass points: east, north, east, read together as east-north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, often written NB, means note well and directs attention to the following text.

clue.text: Confused new boy's name? Not at all!

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled and must be sorted out

parts.note: the word boys, with its s counted

explanation.surface: A muddled lad asks if that is really his name, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges N (new) with BOYS and NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, meaning certainly not.

clue.text: Metal bands on sticks and canes, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word for canes is said out loud and gives a different spelling

parts.note: ferules are canes or rulers once used to punish schoolchildren

explanation.surface: Bands of metal fitted to walking sticks and canes seem to be described.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties 'sticks and canes' together, but 'canes' is the word heard: a ferule, one R, is a punishment cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring or cap of metal fitted on the end of a stick or umbrella strengthens it.

clue.text: Snake and dog in famous row

parts.note: a boa is a snake
to dog someone is to follow or trace them

explanation.surface: A snake and a dog in a well-known argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is rowing: the annual Oxford v Cambridge race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual Oxford against Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames is the most famous rowing race in Britain.

clue.text: Love a Warrant Officer, an entrant in 18

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
an RSM, Regimental Sergeant Major, is a warrant officer in the British Army

explanation.surface: A lover addresses a warrant officer who is competing in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The 18 is the Oxford v Cambridge rowing race at 18 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a rowing race is someone who pulls an oar.

clue.text: Grannie ceremonially embraces her kinswoman

indicators.note: embraces means the run of letters sits inside the two words

explanation.surface: A grandmother formally hugs a female relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a female relative.

clue.text: River holds me right up to the end

indicators.note: holds means the river's name goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: in a down clue up means me and right are read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A river carries the speaker all the way to its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ME plus RT into TREM, which EXE holds.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means the furthest point or limit of something.

clue.text: Mounted like a fish

definitions.meaning: climbed up, as a wall or a peak
covered in the small plates that coat a fish's skin

explanation.definitionFit: Climbing a cliff is to have gone up it, and a fish's skin is covered in small bony plates.

clue.text: Present scoundrel with periodic payment

parts.note: a cur is a mean or worthless man
rent is paid at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Someone gives a rogue a regular sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a verb meaning give but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to now, as in the existing state of affairs.

clue.text: Wood chopped by one

indicators.note: chopped means the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A log is cut by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard dark timber of a tropical tree is the material named.

clue.text: The ram's been trained as a pet

indicators.note: been trained means the letters are drilled into a new order

parts.note: the word rams, the s counted, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A male sheep has been taught to be a household animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been trained' rearranges THE RAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The small rodent is a common cage animal kept by children.

clue.text: Dance with branch office's head

parts.note: a limb is a branch of a tree

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word office

explanation.surface: A dance is staged with the boss of a regional office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branch office' reads as one thing, but 'branch' is LIMB and 'office's head' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean dance has performers bending backwards under a lowered bar.

clue.text: Type of sweet that has no equal

definitions.meaning: a small chocolate drop covered in hundreds and thousands, or the sprinkles themselves
a person or thing without match

explanation.definitionFit: A small chocolate disc topped with sugar sprinkles bears the name, which is French for without equal.

clue.text: Foppish fellow embraced by gorgeous girl

indicators.note: embraced by means the fellow's name is put inside the word for gorgeous girl

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
Andy is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A vain man is hugged by a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is overconcerned with dress, like a dandy, so the adjective means vain about clothes.

clue.text: Value in coppers and shillings

parts.note: the as was a Roman copper coin, plural asses
S is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: Something is priced in pennies and shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' look like British pennies or police, but they are Roman coins: one as, two asses.
explanation.definitionFit: To value something is to judge its worth, as a surveyor does.
